title: Showdown week
text: It's Showdown week and the whole state has picked a side. Workmates won't speak, the papers run a countdown, and the players can feel it at the supermarket.

choices.label: Tell them it's the biggest game in the state

effects.hit_result: A wild week caught up with them by Saturday.

choices.result: The group is up and about. Everyone knows what a loss would mean now.

choices.label: Call it four points, same as any week
choices.result: The board likes the calm. A few players reckon the coach undersold it.

title: The morning after
text: In a two-club town a loss doesn't go away. Talkback is wall-to-wall, the cross-town fans are wearing their colours to work, and the members want to hear from someone.

choices.label: Front the cameras yourself

effects.hit_result: One line got away from you and ran all week.

choices.result: The members saw the coach own it.

choices.label: Shut the doors and review it in-house

effects.why: The players felt protected after a loss

choices.result: The review stays inside the club. Supporters read the silence as not caring.

choices.label: Send {name} out to face them

effects.why: You trusted him to front the city

effects.hit_result: {first} copped the heat for a call that wasn't his.

choices.result: {name} fronts up and says the right things.

title: A Showdown in the pre-season
text: The practice matches have thrown up the cross-town club. It counts for nothing on the ladder, but a big crowd will turn up and both sets of fans will treat it like it does.

choices.label: Pick the best 22 and go hard

effects.hit_result: The Crows won it, and the city knew.
A starter tweaked a hamstring and missed a block of training.

choices.result: The best side goes out to win a game that doesn't count.

choices.label: Play the kids and the fringe

effects.hit_result: The kids lost it, and the city let you hear about it.

choices.result: The young players get a real hit-out in front of a crowd.

title: The kid wants to go home
text: {name} has had a rough few months a long way from his family. His manager rings: the Melbourne clubs are circling and the word "home" keeps coming up.

choices.label: Offer a longer deal with flights home built in

effects.why: You backed him with a longer deal

effects.hit_result: {first} signed. He's staying.
effects.miss_result: {first} hasn't signed. Home is still on his mind.

choices.result: The offer is on the table, and it isn't cheap.

choices.label: Open trade talks with his manager

effects.why: The club set the terms, not the manager
You put him up for trade

choices.result: Talks are open. {first} knows the club will let him go at the right price.

choices.label: Back the program and wait

effects.hit_result: {first} settled on his own. He's starting to call it home.
effects.miss_result: {first} is still homesick, and his manager knows it.

choices.result: No new deal. The club backs its program to settle him.

title: He's named one club
text: {name} has asked for a trade and named a single Victorian club. Everyone knows naming one club drives the price down, and their list manager has stopped returning calls.

choices.label: Hold out to the last hour

effects.hit_result: You held your nerve and got a fair price.
effects.miss_result: Nothing got done. {first} is staying, and he isn't happy.

choices.result: The phones stay quiet until the final hour.

choices.label: Take the deal on the table

effects.why: The group moved on clean

choices.result: It's done, below value. Supporters reckon the club rolled over.

choices.label: Go public about his contract

effects.why: You aired his contract in public
The list saw how the club treats a player who wants out

choices.result: The members side with the club. The rest of the list takes note.

title: Settling the interstate kids
text: Recruiting has brought in four teenagers from interstate. The welfare manager wants money for host families and a trip home every few weeks.

choices.label: Fund the full program
choices.result: The kids settle with host families and train well. It comes out of the football budget.

choices.label: Put them in a share house together

effects.why: The new kids bonded under one roof

effects.hit_result: A late night at the share house made the papers.

choices.result: Four kids, one house, no adult.

title: The local or the best on the board
text: Your pick is up. The best player left is from Victoria. A South Australian kid from the state league, rated a touch lower, grew up with Crows posters on his wall.

choices.label: Take the local kid

effects.why: The recruiters wanted the higher ceiling

choices.result: He'll be here for the long haul. The members love it.

choices.label: Take the best player available

effects.why: You backed the highest ceiling on the board

choices.result: The best talent left is a Crow. Some locals wanted their own boy.

title: The Crows in Melbourne
text: The club's supporters in Melbourne, many of them South Australians who moved for work, want the players at a function the night before the next game over there.

choices.label: Send the whole squad for an hour
choices.result: The Melbourne Crows feel part of the club. It's a late night on the road.

choices.label: Send the captain and two leaders

effects.why: The leaders gave up their night for the supporters

choices.result: The supporters get a few faces. Most of the group rests.

choices.label: Keep the night clear
choices.result: A normal away routine. The supporters who turned up feel snubbed.

title: The state-league clubs feel left behind
text: The South Australian state-league clubs say the Crows take their best kids and give little back. One club president has gone on radio about it.

choices.label: Send your coaches to run their clinics
choices.result: Goodwill across the state, and the scouts see more kids. Your coaches lose a week on the track.

choices.label: Write them a cheque

effects.why: The state-league clubs say the Crows have given back

choices.result: A quick fix. Some reckon it looks like buying them off.

choices.label: Stand your ground on radio
choices.result: The players like a coach who backs the club. The state-league crowd turns sour.

title: Chasing a membership record
text: The board wants a new membership record. Marketing has a plan: the coach's face on every billboard in town.

choices.label: Do the campaign

effects.hit_result: A mid-season dip, and your face is still on the buses.

choices.result: Your face is everywhere. The board is pleased.

choices.label: Put the players on the billboards

effects.hit_result: The extra appearances left a few players flat.

choices.result: The players enjoy it. More appearances, less rest.

choices.label: Say no and let the footy sell it

effects.why: The coach kept the focus on footy

choices.result: The group sees you protect them. The board wanted a team player.

title: Forty degrees
text: Adelaide is in a heatwave and the forecast is 40-plus all week. The fitness staff want the main session kept; the doctor wants it at dawn or cut short.

choices.label: Train at dawn, full load
choices.result: The work gets done before the sun is up. The early starts wear on the group.

choices.label: Cut the session
choices.result: Bodies stay fresh. A week of fitness is gone.

choices.label: Train through the heat

effects.hit_result: The heat took more out of them than it gave.

choices.result: They train in the full heat. It builds hard bodies.

title: The resilience camp
text: An outside firm pitches a pre-season "mental resilience" camp: sleep deprivation, confronting personal sessions, no phones. They say it will forge a premiership group.

choices.label: Book the camp

hit.why: Some of the group came back closer

miss.why: Some of the group came back feeling humiliated

effects.hit_result: Some of the group came home closer.
effects.miss_result: Some players came home feeling humiliated.

effects.hit_result: What went on at the camp leaked to the press.

choices.result: The players hand in their phones and get on the bus.

choices.label: Run your own leadership camp

effects.why: The club ran its own camp

choices.result: Two days away, run by the club. Less drama, two days off the track.

choices.label: No camp, train as normal
choices.result: Full training. The board wanted something done about the group.

title: The quiet side deal
text: A key forward will sign cheap if the club privately promises to trade him to the club of his choice later and tops up his pay through a third party. It's against the rules. Nobody needs to know.

choices.label: Do the deal

effects.hit_result: The league found out. Fines, lost picks, and a board that no longer trusts you.

choices.result: He stays, and he's cheap.

choices.label: Refuse, and pay him properly

effects.why: The club kept its books clean

choices.result: Clean books. The pay squeezes the rest of the list.

choices.label: Refuse, and let him walk
choices.result: Clean books, and a key forward gone.

title: Over to Perth
text: You're off to play {opp} in Perth. Long flight, time difference, hostile crowd. The rivalry was built on these trips.

choices.label: Fly over a day early
choices.result: Bodies settle in Perth. An extra night in the hotel, and some bored players.

choices.label: Fly in the day before
choices.result: A normal week at home and a night with family. The travel sits in the legs.

title: Talkback town
text: Adelaide is a footy town with a lot of radio. After the loss, one host spends an hour asking whether {name} should keep the captaincy.

choices.label: Ring the station and back him live

effects.why: You backed him on air

effects.hit_result: Your call kept the story alive another week.

choices.result: {first} and the group love it. You've fed the story too.

choices.label: Ignore it

effects.why: You said nothing when the radio came for him

effects.hit_result: The story died in two days.
effects.miss_result: The story ran on without you.

choices.result: You leave it alone. {first} wonders why you were quiet.

title: The September tag
text: The papers say the Crows freeze in finals. A columnist has a list of September losses and a theory about the club's mindset.

choices.label: Bring in a sports psychologist

effects.why: The players got tools for finals pressure

effects.hit_result: The press ran it as the Crows calling in the shrink.

choices.result: The players get tools for the pressure.

choices.label: Pin the column to the noticeboard
choices.result: The group is fired up. They burnt energy all week.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.result: Nobody overthinks it. Lose this week and the tag sticks harder.

title: A club great drops in
text: One of the Crows' greats is in town and offers to talk to the group before the weekend.

choices.label: Give him the floor before the main session
choices.result: The room hangs off every word. The session runs late.

choices.label: Have him to lunch with the leaders

effects.why: The leaders learnt what it takes from a club great

choices.result: The leaders soak it up. The rest of the group misses out.

title: The fan favourite's last contract
text: {name} still kicks the goals that bring the house down, but his running numbers are falling. He wants two more years.

choices.label: Give him two

effects.why: You gave him the years he asked for
Two years for an ageing forward ties up a spot the kids wanted

choices.result: The crowd and the group love it. The second year may be a stretch.

choices.label: Offer him one

effects.why: The club paid for form, not memories
He wanted two years and got one

choices.result: A fair deal for both sides. {first} feels a little short-changed.

choices.label: Thank him and let him go

effects.why: The spot goes to the next kid

choices.result: A clean list spot. The supporters are furious.

title: Born to do great things
text: The leadership group wants to rewrite the team's values around the motto on the crest, "born to do great things". It'll take a full afternoon off training.

choices.label: Give them the afternoon

effects.why: The players wrote their own values

choices.result: The group owns its values. The session is gone.

choices.label: Write them yourself over a weekend

effects.why: The coach set the standard in writing
The leaders wanted their own words

choices.result: No training lost. They're your words, not theirs.

title: Kuwarna week
text: The Indigenous players ask to lead a week of the club's football: a session with a Kaurna elder on the meaning of "Kuwarna", the Kaurna word for crow, community visits, and the pre-game talk.

choices.label: Hand them the week

effects.why: The Indigenous players led the club for a week

choices.result: Pride right through the group. Less time on match prep.

choices.label: Keep it to one session

effects.why: The players felt one session sold the week short

choices.result: Normal preparation. The players feel the gesture was small.

title: The country tour
text: The club can take a pre-season game to a country town in South Australia. The locals are thrilled. The ground is rock hard.

choices.label: Go, and play the seniors

effects.hit_result: A starter jarred a knee on the hard ground and missed a block.

choices.result: The whole state hears about it. The ground is as hard as promised.

choices.label: Go, play the kids, seniors run clinics
choices.result: The kids get a game. The town wanted the stars on the field.

choices.label: Stay in the city
choices.result: A safe deck and a full pre-season block. The country feels forgotten.

title: The wine country offer
text: A wine region a short drive from the city offers a big sponsorship. The catch: player appearances at long tastings during the season.

choices.label: Take it, appearances and all

effects.hit_result: A long afternoon at a tasting ended up in the papers.

choices.result: Money for the football department, and long afternoons out.

choices.label: Take it, off-season appearances only
choices.result: Less money, a lukewarm sponsor, and players giving up part of their break.

choices.label: Say no

effects.why: The group stayed on the footy

choices.result: No risk. The board wanted the money.

title: A club great's son
text: The son of a Crows champion has nominated for the draft as a father-son. He's a project: two years away, maybe three.

choices.label: Take him as a father-son

effects.why: The pick could have bought a ready-made player

choices.result: The family ties hold. The members love it.

choices.label: Let him go to the open draft

effects.why: You kept the pick for the best player available

choices.result: You keep your pick. It looks cold to the club's old families.

title: One voice or two
text: The club has run co-captains before. {name} and another senior player are both ready, and the group is split on who leads.

choices.label: Make them co-captains

effects.why: You shared the captaincy
Both leaders kept a voice

choices.result: Both stay happy. In a tough week there may be two messages.

choices.label: Give {name} the captaincy alone

effects.why: You made him the one voice

choices.result: One clear voice. The other senior player feels passed over.

title: The cheer squad's banner
text: The cheer squad wants a Showdown banner that takes a swipe at {opp}. It's funny, it's sharp, and the other mob will see it.

choices.label: Let it run
choices.result: The crowd and the players love it. {opp} come out breathing fire.

choices.label: Ask them to tone it down

effects.why: The cheer squad feels the club gagged them

choices.result: No extra fire for {opp}. The cheer squad grumbles.
